governingDotPoints.text: Solve linear equations up to 2 steps

topic.title: Equations
topic.blurb: Solving linear equations and simple quadratics.

scope.decision: earliest applicable course/topic in skill.stage; confirm against title, blurb and prerequisites

sources.locator: Identify inverse operations; Solving Two-Step Equations paired example 2x+8=14 and x/2-3=1; adjacent guided practice and Key Ideas
sources.observation: Read the inverse-operation diagrams, paired complete solutions, guided practice and Key Ideas. The ordinary examples undo addition/subtraction before multiplication/division because those are the actual outside operations in those forms; both sides receive the inverse operation.
sources.adjustments: Adapted the two available worked examples to 4x+9=37 and x/6-5=3 in workedExamples[0], preserving their paired multiplication/division contrast and line-by-line equalities. Selected distinct coefficients, constants, right-hand sides, intermediate values and results within each task. Replaced blanket add/subtract-first theory wording with the actual-operation rule; retained all three correct existing steps.

sources.locator: Solve two-step equations with negative coefficients: 3-2x=15 and -4-x/2=3; guided practice and Key Ideas
sources.observation: The worked examples undo the constant before dividing or multiplying by the negative number. The Key Ideas identify a negative multiplication/division. This supports negative coefficients as a signed-number case of inverse operations, rather than adding an advanced equation method.
sources.adjustments: Adapted 3-2x=15 to 5-3x=26 in workedExamples[1], giving -7 by division by -3. Retained the existing negative grouped quiz task and rewrote all of its distractors to match specific incorrect operations. Changed the out-of-scope three-operation development task to -6(m+4)=42, combining the taught negative-number case with the grouped outside-first method.

sources.locator: Identify outside/inside inverse operations; Solving Two-Step Equations involving Grouping paired examples 3(x+1)=15 and (x+3)/2=5; guided practice and Key Ideas
sources.observation: Read the outside-first rule, operation diagrams, complete grouping examples, guided practice and Key Ideas. A bracket is grouping; the outside multiplication or division is undone before the addition or subtraction inside. The fraction bar groups the whole numerator.
sources.adjustments: Adapted 3(x+1)=15 to 4(x+3)=52 in workedExamples[3]. Combined the ordinary fraction-bar and grouped numerator examples into the contrasting pair x/4+6=9 and (x+6)/4=9 in workedExamples[5]; these are different placements, not different numerical cases. Corrected the theory claim that a bracket itself is the last operation. Replaced (x+4)/3=2 with (x+5)/3=4 so the solution is not coincidentally equal to the right-hand side.

sources.locator: Solve equations with brackets: left worked example 3(x+4)=21 and Key Ideas allowing divide-first or expand-first; right example and harder guided cases explicitly outside this skill
sources.observation: The left worked example multiplies every inside term, then subtracts the expanded constant and divides the coefficient. The adjacent Key Ideas explicitly allow dividing first or expanding first. The right worked example adds another pronumeral term, so its expand-and-collect scope is not permission to extend this two-operation skill.
sources.adjustments: Adapted the left worked example to 4(x+5)=23 in workedExamples[4], retaining expansion and an exact fraction at the final line. Replaced mastery 4(x-5)+4x=20 and quiz 3(x+4)+5x=44 with single-bracket tasks 5(x-7)=38 and 5(x+7)=23. Preserved each question position, quiz ID and mastery marker; explicitly required expansion where it is the assessed method.

sources.locator: Mixed Practice: Example Solve equations of up to two steps, first row 4x/7=-12 with multiply-by-7 then divide-by-4 working
sources.observation: The complete worked example applies multiplication by the denominator followed by division by the coefficient, retaining an equation at each line. The adjacent Your Turn items use the same two-operation multiplication/division approach.
sources.adjustments: Adapted 4x/7=-12 to 5x/3=17 in workedExamples[2], with exact result 51/5. Replaced the shortcut-friendly mastery equation 147x/13=1470 with 7x/4=19, exact answer 76/7, so equal factors do not hide the two operations.

sources.locator: Equivalent Equations: Multiplying every term; unbalanced/balanced image5.png and image6.png; paired multiplication/division example and Key Ideas
sources.observation: Read the every-term rule, paired complete equivalent-equation examples and Key Ideas, and visually inspected both balance images. The unbalanced image doubles only the x tiles; the balanced image doubles both the x tiles and all unit tiles on both sides. This directly supports diagnosing a next step which leaves a constant unchanged.
sources.adjustments: Adapted the equivalent-equation teaching into workedExamples[6], checking the claimed x+3=55 step from x/5+3=11 against x+15=55. Used different numbers and a question about an incorrect step, not a copied published practice card. Repaired the existing incorrect-next-step quiz numbers and made all option reasons explicitly distinguish equivalent steps from the one invalid step.

review.independentSolution: 4x+7=19. Subtract 7: 4x=12. Divide by 4: x=3. Substitution gives 12+7=19.
review.observation: Both inverse operations are necessary. The given working follows the ordinary outside-addition-first source method.
Correct subtraction inverse and coefficient division; concise two-step working.

review.independentSolution: 26=3x+8. Subtract 8: 18=3x. Divide by 3: 6=x, so x=6. Check 18+8=26.
review.observation: Pronumeral on the right does not change the inverse operations. Reordering the equality to x=6 is valid.

review.independentSolution: x/4+3=10. Subtract 3: x/4=7. Multiply by 4: x=28. Check 7+3=10.
review.observation: Correct multiplication to undo division; the fraction bar contains only x.

review.independentSolution: x/5-2=1. Add 2: x/5=3. Multiply by 5: x=15. Check 3-2=1.
review.observation: Correct two inverses, including an integer answer from a fraction equation. No rounding is required.

review.independentSolution: 6+x/3=4. Subtract 6: x/3=-2. Multiply by 3: x=-6. Check 6-2=4.
review.observation: Constant-first presentation and negative answer are supported by Stage 4 signed-number prerequisites.

review.independentSolution: 3(x+2)=21. Divide by 3: x+2=7. Subtract 2: x=5. Check 3(7)=21.
review.observation: Outside multiplication is undone before the addition inside; the solution does not treat the bracket as an operation.
Correct grouping and subtraction inverse; source outside-first sequence is preserved.
Negative solution is handled with ordinary inverse operations and the supplied exact working is correct.
Exact fraction is appropriate; coefficient 2 does not cancel before the final operation.
Correct negative fraction in simplest form; no decimal approximation is needed.
Correct grouped numerator and signed arithmetic; useful contrast with the positive grouped equation.

review.independentSolution: 3(x+9)=20. Expand first: 3x+27=20. Subtract 27: 3x=-7. Divide by 3: x=-7/3. Check 3(-7/3+9)=20.
review.observation: Explicit expansion-first instruction is fulfilled. Distributive-law rewriting introduces no extra pronumeral term or later-stage collection.

review.independentSolution: 3x/2=9. Multiply by 2: 3x=18. Divide by 3: x=6. Check 18/2=9.
review.observation: Both multiplication/division operations are undone; method is supported by the source mixed-practice example.

review.independentSolution: 7(a+8)=30. Expand: 7a+56=30. Subtract 56: 7a=-26. Divide by 7: a=-26/7. Substitution gives 7(-26/7+8)=30.
review.observation: Expansion keeps whole numbers until the last line, as requested; dividing by 7 first would introduce 30/7 earlier. Both strategy and exact result are provided.

review.independentSolution: For a/3+5=7: subtract 5 to get a/3=2, then multiply by 3, giving a=6. For (a+5)/3=7: multiply by 3 to get a+5=21, then subtract 5, giving a=16. Checks: 6/3+5=7 and (16+5)/3=7.
review.observation: Both equations are solved and the grouping difference is explained. Same displayed numbers serve a deliberate conceptual contrast; different results expose the placement of the fraction bar.
Unique correct answer and all distractor reasons are mathematically consistent.

review.observation: Right-hand pronumeral placement is harmless; each distractor reason is specific and correct.

24 stops at 6x=24; actual right side is 147.
18 is 24-6 instead of 24/6; actual right side is 111.

review.observation: Grouping order and each distractor explanation are correct.

options.observation: 4 is 8-4 instead of 8+4 after dividing by 3; substitution gives 0.
25 follows the erroneous replacement of division by 3 with subtraction: x-4=24-3=21, then add 4. It does not solve the original; why identifies that error.

review.observation: Multiplication/division pair is solved correctly; each reason matches its option.

options.observation: 60 stops at 4x=60 instead of dividing by 4.
5 is 20/4, omitting the multiplication by denominator 3.
240 is 20 times 3 times 4, multiplying rather than dividing by coefficient 4 at the second inverse.

review.independentSolution: (x+5)/3=4. Multiply by 3: x+5=12. Subtract 5: x=7. Check 12/3=4.
review.observation: Fraction bar groups the numerator, so outside division is undone first. All requested work is present.

review.independentSolution: -6(m+4)=42. Divide by -6: m+4=-7. Subtract 4: m=-11. Check -6(-7)=42.
review.observation: Two actual operations only; negative outside coefficient combines grouping with established signed-number knowledge.

review.independentSolution: 5(x-7)=38. Expand: 5x-35=38. Add 35: 5x=73. Divide by 5: x=73/5. The subtraction of 7 happens before multiplication by 5. Adding 7 to both sides yields 5x-28=45, so it does not undo that inside subtraction. One must undo the outside multiplication first, or expand and then add 35.
review.observation: Both requested parts are answered: expansion-first solution and explanation of the incorrect immediate addition. This remains a single-bracket two-operation task, with no extra pronumeral collection.

review.independentSolution: 7x/4=19. Multiply by 4: 7x=76. Divide by 7: x=76/7. Check (7 times 76/7)/4=19.
review.observation: Exact answer and both operations are retained; distinct factors avoid a shortcut hiding the structure.

review.independentSolution: 3x+5=26 -> 3x=21 -> x=7. The only solution option is 7.
review.observation: Unique marked answer is correct; all three distractor reasons describe their stated incorrect operations.

options.observation: x=7 gives 3(7)+5=26 and answers the stem.
31/3 comes from adding 5 to 26 rather than subtracting: (26+5)/3. It gives left side 36, so is not the solution; why is accurate.
21 is the value of 3x after subtracting 5, not x. Its substitution gives 68; why correctly identifies stopping early.
18 comes from 21-3 rather than 21/3; substitution gives 59. The supplied reason accurately identifies subtraction instead of division.

review.independentSolution: x/6+4=11. Subtract 4 from both sides: x/6=7. Multiply both sides by 6: x=42. Check: 42/6+4=7+4=11. The invalid partial multiplication described by option 3 gives x+4=66 -> x=62; applying multiplication to every term instead gives x+24=66 -> x=42.
review.observation: Fresh independent re-solution and all four reasons checked. Exactly x=42 solves the stem. The revised fourth why accurately describes multiplying the x/6 term and right side by 6 while omitting multiplication of the constant 4; it therefore produces the stated wrong equation and distractor value. The original misleading only-right-side description is gone. Correct solution, options, order, ID and scope are preserved.

options.observation: x=42 gives 42/6+4=11 and is the unique correct answer.
x=7 stops at x/6=7, not x=7. Substitution gives 31/6, not 11. The why accurately identifies stopping before multiplying by 6.
x=7/6 divides the quotient 7 by 6 instead of multiplying it. Substitution gives 151/36, not 11. The why accurately describes this wrong inverse.

x=62 solves x+4=66, made by multiplying x/6 and 11 by 6 while incorrectly leaving constant 4 unchanged. The new why says exactly that. Its original left side is 62/6+4=43/3, not 11; every-term multiplication would give x+24=66 and x=42.

review.observation: Expansion instruction is fulfilled and distractors diagnose distinct errors.

options.observation: 23/4 comes from incorrect expansion 4x+3=26, omitting multiplication of the constant; reason matches.
19/2 is (26+12)/4 after wrongly adding 12 rather than subtracting; reason matches.
13/2 stops at x+3=26/4=13/2 before subtracting 3; reason matches.

review.independentSolution: 5(x+7)=23. Expand: 5x+35=23 -> 5x=-12 -> x=-12/5. No fraction occurs until the last line.
review.observation: The requested expansion strategy and exact result are correct; distractors and reasons remain within this method.

options.observation: 16/5 follows faulty expansion 5x+7=23; constant was not multiplied.

review.independentSolution: Original x/6+4=11 gives x=42. The four candidate equations give x=42, x=42, x=62, and x=42 respectively. Hence only x+4=66 is an incorrect next step.
review.observation: The negative stem asks for the invalid step. Exactly the third marked option answers it; the other three equations are mathematically equivalent but do not answer that stem. All reasons are accurate.

options.observation: x+24=66 multiplies every term by 6 and has solution 42. It is a correct next step, so it does not answer which step is incorrect. The why correctly calls it equivalent.
2x+48=132 multiplies every term by 12 and has solution 42. It is equivalent, so fails the negative stem. The why is accurate.
x+4=66 omits multiplying constant 4 by 6 and changes the solution to 62. It is invalid and is therefore the correct response to the incorrect-step stem.
x/6=7 subtracts 4 from both sides and gives 42. It is a valid next step and thus not the answer to the negative stem. The why is accurate.

review.observation: Negative outside coefficient and inside subtraction are undone correctly; all distractor reasons are accurate.

options.observation: 25 follows division by positive 3 rather than negative 3, giving a-21=4. Its original left side is -12, not 12.
-25 follows subtracting 21 from -4 rather than adding it after a-21=-4; original left side is 138.
-4 stops at a-21=-4 and confuses the grouped value with a; original left side is 75.
